---
title: "A vocabulary test: 500 respondents, 13 words"
subtitle: "Catalog A-04 and A-05"
description: "A Rasch model with a Dirichlet process mixture for ability: the prior on alpha changes how many ability groups the model uses, from 3.5 to 9 in expectation."
toc: false
---

The third application is psychometric. A 13-word vocabulary checklist (Open-Source Psychometrics
Project, via the Item Response Warehouse) is fitted with a Rasch model whose ability
distribution is a Dirichlet process mixture, for 500 respondents. The elicited statement is
"about five latent groups, between 2 and 10 with 80% probability".

```{=html}
<div id="w-rasch-k" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/rasch-kpmf.js"></script>

```

- **The prior sets the number of groups.** The posterior mean of K_500 is 3.51 under the
  literature default Gamma(1, 3), 4.43 under Vague (95% interval [2, 10]), 6.73 under the
  Dual-Anchor prior ([3, 12]) and 8.99 under the hard bound ([5, 14]).
- **The elicited range holds under the soft priors.** Pr(2 ≤ K ≤ 10) is .97 to .99 for Vague,
  Gamma(1, 3) and TSMM, .94 for Dual-Anchor, and .74 for the hard bound.
- **A target of 25 is pulled back.** The Count-25 sensitivity (TSMM with mu_K = 25) ends at 11.72:
  the data can move K, but not all the way.
- E(alpha | y) runs from 0.38 (Gamma(1, 3)) to 2.00 (the hard bound, nearly a point mass).

## The groups change, the person scores do not

The same fits describe the ability distribution and score the people. Below, the fitted
densities follow the priors checked above. Neither the distribution nor the 500 respondents'
scores move with the prior; only the number of groups does.

```{=html}
<div id="w-rasch-dens" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/bundles/rasch-density.js"></script>
<script>
  (function () {
    var q = new URLSearchParams(location.search), spec = {}, dens;
    if (q.get("preset")) spec.preset = q.get("preset");
    spec.onSelect = function (on) { if (dens) dens.update({ on: on }); };
    window.__dpxRaschK = DPX["rasch-kpmf"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-rasch-k"), spec);
    dens = DPX["rasch-density"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-rasch-dens"), {});
    window.__dpxRaschDens = dens;
  })();
</script>
```

- **The ability distribution** is the same under every prior: the fitted densities differ from
  the Vague one by at most .002. The stronger priors use more groups to describe the same shape.
  The Gaussian benchmark (grey) is flatter.
- **The person scores** stay put: a score group's posterior ability moves by .031 logits under the
  Dual-Anchor prior, and the WLE scores by at most .006. The 63 perfect scores have a WLE SE of
  1.73, the widest in the sample.
